{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Eight clauses are compliant and require no redline — the mutual liability cap (§21), our assignment and change-of-control rights (§24), the licence grant (§13), audit rights against us (§22), auto-renewal mechanics (§8.2–8.3), Vendor's performance warranty and remedy stack (§19), Vendor insurance (§18), and the absence of any Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

Ten items require action, and they cluster in three places:

- **Restrictive covenants and commercial lock-in.** Section 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights," with no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement. Section 7.2 imposes a Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN. The two Sections 12.4 impose a term-plus-24-month non-compete (including an acquisition bar that functions as sole-sourcing) and a one-way 24-month non-solicit/no-hire. Each of these fails the applicable fallback on every element, and each directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume, exclusivity, most-favoured-customer or no-hire commitment.
- **Missing clauses.** There is no indemnity at all — Section 20 is absent, yet §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to it. There are also no exit obligations: no committed transition assistance and no duty to return, export or delete Customer Data (§16.5 refers Customer Data out to a Section 11 that does not exist).
- **Deliverables and forum.** Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable with only a revocable, term-limited licence back to us, so we lose bespoke reports, configurations and integrations we paid for at term end. Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, outside our accepted list and in conflict with Section 28.2's New York County forum.

All findings passed verification. The termination-for-convenience redline was auto-repaired during drafting (new §9.4 inserted between 9.3 and 9.5 so the Section 2.1 cross-reference resolves) and should be re-read before it goes out.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position we take |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Take the fallback: leave Vendor's Deliverable ownership intact but upgrade our licence to perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free to use, modify and sublicense. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1–21.4 | No redline. Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims outside the cap. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1–24.4 | No redline. At or above preferred; §24.4 removes the change-of-control walk-away trigger. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.1 | No redline. No Customer-payable liquidated or penal amounts anywhere. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1–13.3 | No redline. §14.2 revocability addressed once under IP, not double-flagged. |
| 6 | High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Preferred: delete the Customer-side disclose-and-match obligation. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (p0046) | Preferred: convert the term-plus-24-month prohibition into an express permission. |
| 8 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (p0045) | Preferred: remove the one-way 24-month non-solicit/no-hire; mutual 12-month fallback available if needed. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation *(redline repaired)* | § 2.1; new § 9.4 | Add Customer 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees, bar Vendor convenience termination, conform §2.1. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1–22.3 | No redline. Meets preferred in full, including off-site independent auditor and no direct system access. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Preferred: New York law; delete the Singapore forum so §28.2's New York County venue stands alone. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Preferred: replace the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with an express no-minimum-commitment statement (§7.1 already covers the pricing element). |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2–8.3 | No redline. 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 | Preferred: six months' assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1–19.5 | No redline. Meets and in places exceeds preferred; disclaimer does not swallow express warranties. |
| 16 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (p0046) | Preferred: delete the "acquire" prong only, which operates as a de facto sole-supplier obligation. |
| 17 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 9.3 (refers to absent § 20.5) | Preferred: insert Vendor indemnity as new §20 (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with procedure and a narrow Customer indemnity; no super-cap, to preserve §21.3. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1–18.2 | No redline. CGL, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, term plus one year, certificates on request. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating chips:

1. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay / no convenience exit (MINCOMMIT, T4C).** A three-year USD 2,000,000 per year commitment with no reduction or termination rights, and no Customer convenience right anywhere in a multi-year term.
2. **§ 7.2 Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended as to product, no time limit, no like-for-like carve-outs.
3. **§ 12.4 non-compete and exclusivity (p0046).** Undefined competing scope, any territory, term plus 24 months; the acquisition prong bars us from procuring competing services with no performance-based exit.
4. **§ 12.4 non-solicit/no-hire (p0045).** One-way, all Vendor employees, 24 months post-term, no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
5. **§ 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction.** Outside our accepted list and internally inconsistent with § 28.2.
6. **Missing Vendor indemnity (§ 20 absent).** No IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity, despite four cross-references assuming one exists.
7. **Missing exit obligations (§ 10).** No committed transition assistance and no duty to return, export or delete Customer Data — the risk of no data return on exit.

Items 1–4 each contradict Section 12.3, in which Vendor already acknowledges we made no such commitments; we should lead with that inconsistency.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten action items, with `[Playbook]` comments explaining each change and the fallback where one exists (mutual 12-month non-solicit; 90-day transition assistance with 30-day export).
2. **Re-read the § 9.4 convenience-termination insert** before circulation — that redline was repaired to place the new clause between §§ 9.3 and 9.5 so the § 2.1 cross-reference resolves, and to preserve the no-reduction restriction in § 2.1.
3. **Escalate the commercial terms** in § 2.1 (three-year take-or-pay) to the business owner, since the volume commitment and the convenience-exit ask are linked and may require a pricing trade.
4. **Point Vendor to § 12.3** as the fastest route to resolving §§ 2.1, 7.2 and both §§ 12.4 — those covenants are inconsistent with Vendor's own acknowledgement.
5. **Ask Vendor to supply its standard indemnity** for insertion at § 20, and flag the dangling cross-references (§ 9.3 to § 20.5; § 16.5 to a non-existent § 11) as drafting defects to be cured in the same turn.
6. **Confirm no further changes** to the eight compliant clauses; if Vendor reopens the § 21 cap, § 24 assignment rights or § 19 warranties, treat that as a new deviation and re-run the review.
"}
